title: Plan hard jobs only; count later-caused failures in keep rule
summary: Replace the boolean job_plan switch with a hard-jobs-only mode in athena.toml, so the run pipeline plans and critiques only when the reading is marked hard. Extend the keep rule (job-planning.md section 9) and athena status to count, per planned and unplanned landing, later failures, reverts or fix jobs citing them. This follows job 20261027-054211-a2n5, whose landed refusal rule showed landed share is the wrong measure. Audience: Sri and the operators who read athena status.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for planning dispatch and status counts; cargo test, clippy -D warnings and fmt pass.
Criteria run tests that exercise hard versus ordinary readings and the status output.
The keep rule now measures later harm, not only landed share.
Hard-only planning is enforced by config and run code, tested.
Docs and decisions explain the change and why for an outside reader.
One focused change across the listed files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Job 20261027-054211-a2n5 is cited as the motivating case. Its two findings (broad governance keywords, separate keyword test table) concern reading.rs governance matching and are not part of this request. They are out of scope and remain unaddressed here.
The config gains a mode setting (for example mode = "hard") in [job_plan] in place of or alongside enabled; the existing enabled=false stays a full off switch.

Hardness comes from the existing hard marking in the reading, which already escalates the producer. reading.rs only gets a hardness definition (rule that can refuse or hold work, landing, history check, records, run pipeline, drain) if the marking lacks it.
A later cause is read from existing records: failure introspections, revert records and fix jobs citing a landed job id. No new record kind is added unless none exists.
athena.toml is a governance file and is a named deliverable here.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a test loads athena.toml (planning for hard jobs only), and shows a reading marked hard runs the planner and critic while an ordinary reading runs neither.
Run cargo test: a test shows athena status reports, separately for planned and unplanned landings, how many were later cited as the cause of a failure, revert or fix job, beside the landed share.
athena.toml [job_plan] is set so planning runs for hard jobs only (git diff shows the change), and crates/athena-data/src/config.rs parses and validates the setting.
docs/design/job-planning.md section 9 and docs/decisions.md record the new keep-rule measure, the hard-only planning, and why, citing job 20261027-054211-a2n5.
The hard definition in code or docs covers rules that refuse or hold work, landing, the history check, records, the run pipeline and drain.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the change.

out_of_scope: Fixing the two findings of job 20261027-054211-a2n5 (broad governance keywords, KEYWORD_REQUESTS table)
Changing defaults.toml, workflows or other governance files besides athena.toml
Changing the planner or critic prompts, caps or max_rounds
Reverting or reworking the refusal rule job 20261027-054211-a2n5 landed
departures: Hard job touching run pipeline, config and status across about eight files, so cost and time are above the reference.
urgent_reason: Cuts wasted work from unplanned jobs landing rules that stopped drains, which cause failed drains and redo work.
hard_reason: Changes the run pipeline and the keep rule that judges other jobs, and defines which jobs are hard.
